marks.gloss_en: 'today and tomorrow' -- today like tomorrow: as tomorrow has its night with it, so today has its night with it; today's night had already passed, so two [full] days besides today -- hence the added day
ומנלן דהסכים? דלא שראי שכינה עד צפרא דשבתא -- the Shechina came on Shabbat morning, after the added day
the Shechina did not rest [on Sinai] until Shabbat morning
Israel, with whom the Shechina spoke only once and at a fixed time, were told 'do not approach a woman'; I, with whom it speaks at every hour and at no fixed time -- all the more so
ומנלן? דכתיב לך אמר להם שובו לכם לאהליכם, וכתיב בתריה ואתה פה עמד עמדי
ואית דאמרי: פה אל פה אדבר בו
'go say to them: return to your tents', and after it 'and you, stand here with Me' (Deuteronomy 5)
the Pesach, one of the 613 mitzvot -- the Torah said 'no stranger shall eat of it' (Ex 12:43); the whole Torah, with Israel apostate -- all the more so
ומנלן? שנאמר אשר שברת, ואמר ריש לקיש: יישר כחך ששברת
Reish Lakish: 'which you broke' (Ex 34:1) -- asher: may your strength be firm, that you broke [them]
דתניא: שלשה דברים עשה משה מדעתו והסכים הקדוש ברוך הוא עמו... הוסיף יום אחד מדעתו (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names a bare דתניא)
אמר לך רבי יוסי: יום אחד הוסיף משה מדעתו (= p_moshe_hosif_yom), דתניא...
Moses added one day of his own accord
לכדתניא: וישב משה את דברי העם... ויגד משה את דברי העם -- what passed between them was (per R' Yosei b. R' Yehuda) the mitzva of hagbala (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names כדתניא)
[for the Rabbanan] 'the third' -- to what? to the matter that is taught [in the baraita on Ex 19:8-9]
דכתיב וישב משה -- משבבין דעתו; דכתיב ויגד משה -- מושכין לבו כאגדה
דכתיב וישב משה -- משיבין דעתו; דכתיב ויגד משה -- קשין כגידין
what the Holy One said to Moses, Moses to Israel, Israel to Moses, and Moses reported back -- this is the mitzva of setting bounds; the words of R' Yosei b. R' Yehuda
'sanctify them today and tomorrow' -- two days of separation; but R' Yosei has them separate on Wednesday for a Shabbat giving, three days
R' Yosei: on Tuesday He told them the mitzva of setting bounds
'be ready for the third day' -- the giving on the third day of separation, against R' Yosei's four
הא אמרינן: יום אחד הוסיף משה מדעתו (= p_moshe_hosif_yom)
the third of the month was the third of the week, so the month began on Sunday -- against the Rabbanan's Monday
אמרי לך רבנן: הא מני -- רבי יוסי היא (= p_bar_shlishi_kery)
the verse: 'and be ready for the third day' (Ex 19:11)
the sixth of the month was the sixth of the week, so the month began on Sunday -- against the Rabbanan
הא נמי רבי יוסי היא (= p_bar_shishi_kery)
the baraita: 'sixth' -- the sixth of the month, the sixth [day] of the week (so the month began on Sunday)
